fix: Run the 9:16 crop, or reshoot with the strip longer than the frame: 'the bracelet is longer than the frame is tall; the top and bottom edges of the frame each cut through a stone; no clasp and no end anywhere in frame; about 12-14 stone units visible'. If the bands must read as 6 cm: 'each powder band about seven stone-units deep'.

It is held down because the pastel seeds still camouflage the stones in the bowl, the defocused back of the curl reads as a jumble of silver galleries, the bright cream bowl competes with the product, and the top is greyed rather than clean blush.

fix: End the strand on the linen in the opened fold-over box clasp half (rectangular frame with hinged latch plate), or run the spill off the frame's lower-left edge. Keep every unit face-up in the curl. Use a shallower layer of seeds, or ivory/white seeds in the bowl, so the stones sit proud and read as the brightest thing. A high-key pale blush backdrop, not grey-mauve. Keep the low warm sun and hard kicker.

reasons: Scale vs the closed loop (referent: an 18 cm bracelet is ~62 mm across outer, ~7.75 unit widths). Measured with the front A unit rotated level, a face-on unit is 123.5 px outer (stone 82.5 px, ratio 0.67), with a pitch of ~127.5 px. The loop's outer extremes are at x~454 (y~1175) and x~1038 (y~890), 584 px across and ~650 px along the tilted major axis. So the loop is only ~5.3 unit widths across (~5.5 after allowing ~5% for the front units sitting nearer the camera), vs ~7.75: units are +40-47% too big for the loop. At true 8 mm units the loop is ~42-44 mm across, a bracelet of only ~11 cm.

Count agrees: the front arc between the two side-on extremes holds P A P A Y A P, ~6.4 pitches, so the whole loop is ~12.7 pitches, about 12 stones plus clasp vs 20 plus clasp (-40%). This is the same failure as r1's P04_a1 (4.8-5.0 unit widths), only slightly improved.

Halo finish (would also need fixing): matched at the same unit size against listing-7, each halo is a field of ~1-px micro-dots that reads as grey stippled metal. Listing-7 shows about 2 rows of distinct, bright clear pave stones (~1/7 of the unit wide); P02/P05 show fine but sparkling pave. Overall brightness is similar (halo mean luminance 140 vs 143-155 on listing-7), so this is texture, not exposure. At phone size the halos read as dull grey frames rather than a pave halo.
